scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland): Establishment of Large RAS Culture System Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 29, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY is designed to enhance fish production and productivity through various interventions. 

It focuses on the sustainable development of the fisheries sector while ensuring the welfare of fishers and fish farmers. 

The scheme is part of the broader Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative aimed at making India self-reliant. 

The PMMSY has a total outlay of ₹20,050 crores for a period of five years from 2020 to 2025. 

One of the key components of PMMSY is the establishment of large Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) in various states, including Gujarat. 

The objective of establishing large RAS culture systems is to increase fish production through modern aquaculture practices. 

The RAS technology allows for efficient water use and higher stocking densities. 

It also enables year-round fish production irrespective of climatic conditions. 

The specific target for fish production under PMMSY is to achieve an increase of 70 lakh metric tonnes by 2024-25. 

In Gujarat, the establishment of large RAS culture systems is expected to contribute significantly to this target. 

The benefits of the PMMSY include financial assistance for setting up RAS units. 

The government provides up to 40% of the project cost as a subsidy for individual entrepreneurs. 

For SC/ST entrepreneurs, the subsidy can go up to 60% of the project cost. 

The maximum assistance for setting up RAS units can be up to ₹2 crores. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It is estimated that the PMMSY will generate around 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs. 

Eligibility criteria for availing benefits under the PMMSY include being an Indian citizen. 

Applicants must be involved in fish farming or related activities. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants. 

However, applicants must have a minimum educational qualification of Class 8. 

The application process for the PMMSY involves several steps. 

Interested individuals must submit an application to the respective state fisheries department. 

The application should include details about the proposed project and the applicant's background. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Additionally, a project report outlining the proposed RAS system must be submitted. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the state fisheries department. 

After approval, the applicant will receive a sanction order for the subsidy. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is released after the approval of the project. 

Subsequent installments are released upon verification of progress. 

The implementing authority for the PMMSY in Gujarat is the Fisheries Department of the Government of Gujarat. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the scheme. 

It also provides technical support and guidance to beneficiaries. 

Contact details for the Fisheries Department can be found on the official government website. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of research and development in aquaculture. 

It encourages the adoption of innovative technologies in fish farming. 

The scheme promotes the establishment of fish feed mills and hatcheries. 

These facilities are crucial for ensuring the availability of quality fish seeds and feed. 

The PMMSY also aims to enhance the marketing of fish products. 

It supports the development of fish markets and cold chain infrastructure. 

This is essential for reducing post-harvest losses and improving the income of fishers. 

The scheme also includes provisions for skill development and training. 

Training programs are conducted for fish farmers to improve their knowledge and skills. 

The PMMSY has a strong focus on women empowerment in the fisheries sector. 

It encourages the participation of women in fish farming and allied activities. 

The scheme aims to promote gender equality and enhance the livelihoods of women in fisheries. 

The PMMSY is expected to have a positive impact on the overall economy of Gujarat. 

It is projected to increase the state's fish production significantly. 

This will not only benefit fishers but also contribute to food security. 

The PMMSY aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set by the United Nations. 

It aims to promote sustainable practices in aquaculture and fisheries management. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the income levels of fishers by at least 20%. 

This will improve their standard of living and reduce poverty in fishing communities. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of environmental sustainability. 

It encourages practices that minimize the impact on aquatic ecosystems. 

The establishment of RAS systems is a step towards sustainable aquaculture. 

These systems are designed to reduce water usage and minimize waste. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive initiative that addresses multiple aspects of the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a robust framework for the growth and development of aquaculture in India. 

The scheme is a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

It is expected to position India as a global leader in sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The PMMSY is a vital component of the government's efforts to revitalize the fisheries sector. 

It aims to ensure that the benefits of growth reach the grassroots level. 

The establishment of large RAS culture systems in Gujarat is a key focus area. 

This initiative is expected to set a benchmark for aquaculture practices in the country. 

The PMMSY is a forward-looking scheme that aims to transform the fisheries landscape in India. 

It is an embodiment of the government's commitment to the welfare of fishers and sustainable development. 

The implementation of PMMSY will pave the way for a prosperous future for the fisheries sector in Gujarat and beyond.
